**Updated Understanding:**
When two cities are only 50 km apart yet have different climates, the most plausible cause among the given options is latitude (C). Using a typical environmental lapse rate of about 0.65°C per 1000 m, even a 500 m elevation difference would only yield roughly 0.3°C of temperature change—small relative to latitudinal effects. Since 1° of latitude is roughly 69 km, 50 km corresponds to about 0.72°; with a common latitudinal temperature gradient of ~0.8–1.0°C per degree, that implies ~0.6–0.7°C difference, which is more substantial over this distance. Population and longitude are less likely explanations for climate differences over such a short distance.
